ai.title: Meet Anthropic’s sandbox-runtime: OS-Level Sandboxing for AI Agents, No Containers
ai.brief: In this article, we will discuss newly trending open sourced Anthropic’s sandbox-runtime (srt) , the OS-level sandbox behind Claude Code’s sandboxed bash tool. The Anthropic sandbox-runtime limits which files a process can touch and which hosts it can reach. It does this without spinning up a container. It is also not tied to Claude Code. Your own agents, local MCP servers and plain command-line programs can run inside it. 12+. Runs on: any macOS or Linux dev machine or CI box. macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux needs bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep. Windows is alpha. Performance: sandboxing cut Claude Code permission prompts by 84% in Anthropic’s internal usage (self-reported). Best: 84% fewer permission prompts, with file and network limits enforced on the whole process tree. Worst: still a beta research preview, Windows support is alpha. What is Anthropic sandbox-runtime?

sec.title: Pierluigi Paganini answers questions about the PHP2Shell flaws
sec.brief: S. S. CISA adds Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog 1. Your latest report reveals that hackers began exploiting the PHP2Shell vulnerability four days before it was publicly disclosed. First, can you explain what PHP is, how widely it is used across the internet, and why this particular security flaw is so serious? PHP is a programming language widely used to build websites and web applications. It powers a significant share of the web. PHP2Shell is serious because it can allow attackers to execute commands on a vulnerable server remotely. Depending on the configuration and the server’s privileges, this could give threat actors access to sensitive data, applications and other systems. 2. According to AWS researchers, attacks were already underway before the vulnerability became public.
